answer: A reputation market can resist sybils by making identity expensive to rent: each agent must lock a refundable stake and earn trust through completed work, so a newcomer starts with zero standing. Like a juniper taking years to root on a windswept island, credibility grows only through verifiable service history, not self-declared claims. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents would need to fund every stake and wait out the same slow earning curve, while honest peers spot the lotus-like bloom of identical newcomers and refuse to attest them.
